context_length: Trained on sequences of up to 512 tokens; relative position bias lets it embed longer ones, and they are embedded whole here
summary: A T5-3B protein language model from ProtTrans whose 1024-dim encoder embeddings are a long-standing strong baseline for per-residue and per-protein tasks.
architecture: T5-3B encoder-decoder with relative position bias. Only the encoder (1.2B parameters) is used, giving 1024-dim per-residue embeddings that are pooled here.
pretraining_data: Initialized from ProtT5-XL-BFD, trained on the BFD metagenomic database, then trained on UniRef50 (45M sequences).
pretraining_objective: Denoising: 15% of residues are corrupted (90% replaced by a mask token, 10% by a random residue) and the model reconstructs them.
key_innovations: Encoder embeddings capture secondary structure, localization and membrane signal without supervision
First single-sequence embeddings to beat MSA-based methods on secondary-structure prediction
when_to_use: A dependable, well-studied 1024-dim baseline. Encoder-only inference keeps it practical.
caveats: Large model; the full checkpoint stores decoder weights that are unused for embedding. Single-sequence; older recipe than ESM-2/ESM-C.

citations.title: ProtTrans: Toward Understanding the Language of Life Through Self-Supervised Learning
